## Data Model Signals

### Entities
- **Person/Contact:** id, name (first/last), phone (type: mobile/land-line), email, address (home/property/other), last_communication_at, last_seen_at, avatar_initials, avatar_bg_color
- **SmartList / Pond:** id, name (e.g. "Out Of State Home Owners"), assigned_agent
- **Agent/User:** id, name (Rebecca Peterson, Matt Ryan), avatar_photo
- **Email:** id, from_agent_id, to_contact_id, sent_at, status (DELIVERED / NOT_DELIVERED), subject, body_html/text
- **Note:** id, contact_id, created_by_agent_id, created_at, body_text, source (e.g. "Imported")
- **Task:** id, contact_id, assigned_to, due_at, title, status
- **Appointment:** id, contact_id, scheduled_at, title, location
- **Deal:** id, contact_id, stage, value, created_at
- **ActionPlan:** id, contact_id, plan_name, status (running/stopped), started_at
- **Automation:** id, contact_id, automation_name, status
- **File:** id, contact_id, filename, uploaded_at, uploaded_by
- **Collaborator:** id, contact_id, agent_id, role
- **ListEvent (system event):** contact_id, event_type (Released/Claimed), list_id, by_agent_id, at

### Background / Property Intelligence Fields (Custom Fields or integrated data layer)
- owner_type (e.g. "In-state absentee")
- mailing_city, mailing_state
- property_beds, property_baths, property_sqft, year_built, lot_size_acres
- purchase_date, purchase_price, assessed_value
- equity_pct, ownership_pct
- score_total (integer), score_label (e.g. "COOL")
- score_tenure, score_equity, score_absentee, score_age, score_lot (sub-score integers)
- classification_tag (e.g. "WESTSIDE HOMEOWNER - COOL")
- property_subdivision

### Enum Values Revealed
- **Email delivery status:** DELIVERED, NOT_DELIVERED
- **Phone types:** mobile, land-line
- **Address types:** (home), (Property)
- **Owner types:** In-state absentee
- **Score labels:** COOL (others likely: HOT, WARM, COLD)
- **List event types:** Released, Claimed
- **Activity types:** All, Email, Note, Call, SMS-Sent(?), SMS-Received(?), Starred

### Relationships
- Contact → many Emails (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Notes (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Tasks (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Appointments (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Deals (one-to-many)
- Contact → many ListEvents (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Files (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Collaborators → Agent (many-to-many via join)
- Contact → many ActionPlan instances (one-to-many)
- Contact → many Automations (one-to-many)
- Contact → one SmartList/Pond assignment at a time (with history of claimed/released events)
- Contact → one Background record (property intelligence data, possibly via external data enrichment)

### Non-Obvious Logic / Implementation Notes

1. **"NOT DELIVERED" badge logic:** FUB tracks email delivery status separately per message. When an email bounces or the recipient's server rejects it, the status field is updated to `NOT_DELIVERED` and the badge appears inline in the timeline. The ⓘ icon likely opens a popover with the SMTP bounce reason.

2. **"Person 1 of 874" navigation context:** This implies the user arrived at this contact detail page FROM a list view (likely a smart list or search result). The list context (including the ordered 874-person result set) is preserved in state (URL param or session) so the → keyboard/button navigation can advance through the list without returning to the list view.

3. **Activity filter counts:** The filter bar shows pre-aggregated counts per activity type (0 emails, 1 note, 2 SMS-out, 2 SMS-in, etc.). These are probably computed server-side and returned with the contact detail payload, not recounted on filter click. The "All" filter shows all events regardless of type.

4. **System events (Released / Claimed):** These are FUB "Pond" system events — when a contact is moved between smart lists/ponds by agents. They appear as compact, avatar-less rows in the timeline, distinct from user-generated activities.

5. **Background / Property Intelligence section:** This data is NOT standard FUB contact fields. It appears to be data enriched from a third-party property data provider (BatchData, PropStream, or similar). The score (34 COOL) and sub-scores (Tenure, Equity, Absentee, Age, Lot) look like a lead scoring algorithm output for identifying motivated sellers. These are stored as custom fields in FUB.

6. **AgentFire FUB Widget (collapsed):** AgentFire is a real estate website/IDX platform that offers a FUB widget integration. When expanded, it would show website behavioral data for this contact (pages visited, listings viewed, search filters used). It appears collapsed by default likely because this contact has no AgentFire website activity.

7. **Note "Imported By Matt Ryan":** The "Imported" label suggests this note was not typed manually in FUB but rather bulk-imported (via CSV import or API) from an external data source. This is reflected in the note header labeling it as an import rather than a manually created note.

8. **Avatar initials color:** "GH" initials on teal background — FUB assigns deterministic colors to contacts without photos, likely based on a hash of the contact's name or ID mapped to a predefined color palette.

9. **Financing section:** The "Lender" field is visible but empty. This is a standard FUB field for tracking the contact's mortgage lender/pre-approval source. The Financing section likely contains additional fields (Loan Type, Pre-approval Amount, Pre-approval Expiry) that are collapsed or empty.

10. **The ⚡ (lightning bolt) on Tasks:** This is likely the "Assign Action Plan" quick button — clicking it opens an action plan selector directly from the Tasks panel, which would automatically create a series of tasks based on a predefined action plan template.

11. **Files drag-and-drop:** The "drag some here" text in the Files panel means the entire Files panel card acts as a drop zone. A global dragover handler on the page likely highlights this panel when a file is dragged anywhere over the right column.

12. **"Try Team Mentions" helper:** FUB supports @-mentions of team members in notes to notify them. The helper button either pre-fills "@" in the textarea or opens a tooltip explaining the feature. This is a discoverability affordance for users who haven't used team mentions before.
